subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Drivers of passenger dissatisfaction / complaint experience in airline reviews — i.e., what aspects of the service go wrong and shape negative (vs. positive) sentiment.

per_column.name: primary_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: This is the anchor of the inferred focus: it directly classifies each review by the dominant complaint theme (service_quality, staff_attitude, operational_failures, baggage_handling, etc.), which is precisely a 'what-goes-wrong' decomposition.

per_column.name: sentiment_polarity
per_column.rationale: Relevant but the weakest link: bare valence (negative/positive/neutral) is a generic attribute that partly overlaps with the existing 'Overall Rating' and 'Recommended' fields. It supports the dissatisfaction framing by separating negative from positive experience, but on its own it is the kind of mechanical column that does not by itself realise the focus.

per_column.name: crew_interpersonal_demeanor
per_column.rationale: A well-differentiated facet of the experience focus, refining 'staff_attitude' into behavioural categories (rude_dismissive, indifferent_robotic, professional_attentive). Adds finer granularity than the raw 'Staff Service' rating.

per_column.name: operational_disruption_type
per_column.rationale: A coherent facet capturing operational failure modes (delay, cancellation, missed_connection, rebooking_chaos) with an explicit 'no_disruption' baseline — a strong driver of dissatisfaction not covered by original numeric ratings.

per_column.name: physical_comfort_details
per_column.rationale: Decomposes the comfort dimension into concrete causes (seat_design_legroom, recline_configuration, aircraft_age) with a 'no_issues' baseline; a legitimate driver facet, though partly overlapping with the existing 'Seat Comfort' rating.

per_column.name: cabin_environment_quality
per_column.rationale: Captures cleanliness/maintenance/temperature as an experience facet (dirty_unhygienic, dated_showing_wear). Coherent with the focus, though its ordinal cleanliness scale slightly overlaps conceptually with physical_comfort_details' aircraft condition.

judge.rationale: The added columns are not a random grab-bag: five of six clearly cohere around a single inferable focus — the drivers of (dis)satisfaction / complaint experience — with primary_complaint_category acting as the top-level anchor and crew demeanor, operational disruption, physical comfort, and cabin environment serving as differentiated sub-facets. This is a defensible proposed focus given a query that explicitly declines to name one, and it is genuinely actionable (an airline analyst can rank complaint categories, tie crew behaviour or disruptions to negative sentiment, and prioritise fixes). Two things hold the scores back rather than lifting them to the top band. (1) Coherence is only moderately tight: the set reads partly as an 'enumerate every aspect' decomposition rather than a decisive commitment to ONE aspect the query asked the system to single out, and sentiment_polarity is a generic valence column that duplicates signal already present in Overall Rating/Recommended. (2) Structure quality is dented by partial redundancy — several facet columns (comfort, cabin condition, staff) restate categories already present inside primary_complaint_category, and there is conceptual overlap between physical_comfort_details (aircraft_age) and cabin_environment_quality (dated_showing_wear). Net: a sound, useful, complaint-centred structure that realises the focus-inference intent, but with enough genericness and overlap to keep it out of the highest scoring range.
